Subject: Immediate: Degraded throughput on Dedicated GPU pool — investigating

Hi Jenna —

We detected degraded throughput and elevated queuing on your Dedicated GPU pool for the us-west-2 tenant starting ~08:58 PDT. Our control plane automatically routed a subset of traffic to the hosted fallback tier to preserve availability, but you may have seen higher latency for short periods and a small number of 5xx errors while the fallback completed.

What we know so far: 
- Impact window: ~08:58–09:10 PDT (ongoing investigation)
- Symptoms: sudden queue growth, spikes in per-request latency, increased scheduling retries
- Mitigation in place: tiered fallback active; automated burst capacity enabled

Immediate asks for me: can you confirm if your production telemetry saw any client-side errors or user-impacted sessions? Any specific endpoints more affected than others?

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-incident-log-2026-03-28.csv (initial metrics snapshot)

I'm looping in our on-call infra and your CSM to keep this moving. We will follow up with timeline and next steps in the next 30–60 minutes.

—Rachel

Subject: Re: Fwd: Immediate: Degraded throughput on Dedicated GPU pool — action items

Quick technical summary (post initial investigation):
- Root cause: under a sudden burst of short inference requests we observed allocation thrash in the scheduler due to an interaction between the KV-cache eviction policy and the new multi-tenant packing heuristic. The eviction path caused frequent kernel reloads leading to per-request stalls and a scheduler contention window.
- Immediate fix applied (03/28 10:05 PDT): disabled aggressive packing, increased headroom for the ACME dedicated pool, and widened autoscale thresholds to suppress oscillation. These actions allowed the tiered-fallback to drain the backlog and restored normal throughput by ~09:12 PDT.
- Permanent remediation planned: patch to scheduler to make allocation idempotent, adjust eviction policy to be LRU-preferring for hot keys, and add a short cooldown in the autoscaler. Estimated delivery: week of 2026-04-06.
- Observed impact: ~8 minutes of elevated latency, ~12% user-facing error rate for the most critical endpoints, no data loss.

I've attached the diagnostic logs and a postmortem draft with timeline and measurements. Next internal steps: ship the scheduler patch (INFRA-1542), add regression tests for KV eviction under burst, and update our autoscale runbooks.

Attachments: postmortem-draft-ACME-2026-04-01.md

—Sean

- Incident window: 2026-03-28 08:58–09:12 PDT
- Root cause: allocation/scheduler contention triggered by KV-cache eviction + packing heuristic under burst
- Customer impact: brief increased latency and ~12% transient error rate on specified endpoints; estimated user sessions affected: ~2,100 (global)
- Mitigation performed: temporary pool headroom increase, disabled aggressive packing, enabled fallback routing (completed 09:12 PDT)

Planned near-term actions for ACME:
- Ship scheduler patch and autoscaler cooldown (ETA week of 2026-04-06)
- Run a coordinated load test with ACME to validate patch and thresholds
- Offer SLA credit per contract — Monica will coordinate details

Please let us know if this format answers your internal compliance needs or if you'd like an expanded timeline with raw logs. We're also happy to schedule a 30-minute RCA call with your engineering team; propose a few windows and we'll accommodate.
